hints: Focus on what the word initiation really means, it is the very first step that creates the reactive species to start the chain.
Notice that UV light breaks the weak Cl-Cl bond to make the first radicals, not the strong C-H bond in methane.
Remember to check for homolytic fission with single dots for radicals, and pick the equation that shows one molecule splitting into two identical radicals.
walkthrough:
**Recall the three stages of free radical substitution**

Free radical substitution has initiation, propagation and termination. Initiation is the step where stable molecules are first turned into highly reactive free radicals by UV light.

Overall reaction:
$$\text{CH}_4 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV light}} \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{HCl}$$

**Apply homolytic fission to chlorine**

Initiation needs homolytic fission, where a covalent bond splits evenly and each atom keeps one electron to form two radicals. The Cl-Cl bond is relatively weak and is easily broken by UV light.

Initiation equation:
$$\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV light}} 2\text{Cl}\bullet$$

**Confirm why methane is not involved yet**

Methane does not split in initiation because its C-H bond is much stronger and needs a radical to attack it. Methane first reacts later in the propagation step when a $\text{Cl}\bullet$ radical abstracts a hydrogen.

First propagation step for comparison:
$$\text{Cl}\bullet + \text{CH}_4 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\bullet + \text{HCl}$$

options.A: This shows homolytic fission of $\text{CH}_4$ into $\text{CH}_3\bullet$ and $\text{H}\bullet$. The C-H bond is too strong to be broken by UV light for initiation, and $\text{CH}_3\bullet$ is actually formed later in propagation.
options.B: This shows heterolytic fission of $\text{CH}_4$ into ions, $\text{CH}_3^-$ and $\text{H}^+$. Free radical substitution involves radicals with single dots, not ions with full charges, so this mechanism is wrong.
options.C: This is correct. UV light causes homolytic fission of the Cl-Cl bond, with each Cl atom keeping one electron to form two $\text{Cl}\bullet$ radicals. These radicals then go on to start the propagation chain.
options.D: This shows heterolytic fission of $\text{Cl}_2$ into $\text{Cl}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$. Initiation is homolytic, not heterolytic, so it must form two neutral radicals, not a pair of oppositely charged ions.
